key_insight: This paper shows that raw agent execution traces are too noisy to optimize directly, and that better agent improvement comes from extracting structurally meaningful failure patterns and root causes. In simple terms: compress many messy trajectories into a smaller set of high-value causal signals for reflection-based optimization.
problem_solved: It addresses the difficulty of using long-horizon agent traces for optimization when traces are redundant, heterogeneous, and filled with irrelevant steps. These issues make LLM-based reflection inefficient and can lead to overfitting to low-value failures instead of learning actionable improvements.
method: Group and filter large collections of execution traces to reduce redundancy and focus on informative failures.
Analyze trajectories structurally to identify repeated patterns, key decision points, and failure modes rather than treating every trace equally.
Extract causal root causes from trajectories so the optimizer can target the true sources of agent failure and generate better policy updates.
impact: For practitioners, this can make agent debugging and improvement more sample-efficient, less noisy, and more robust. It helps LLM-based optimizers learn from the right failures instead of being distracted by irrelevant trace details.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing noisy traces flowing into structural analysis and then into causal root-cause extraction.

A causal graph or flowchart linking symptoms, intermediate states, and root causes.
paper_title: From Noisy Traces to Root Causes: Structural Trajectory Analysis and Causal Extraction for Agent Optimization
paper_authors: Ying Chang, Jiahang Xu, Xuan Feng, Chenyuan Yang, Peng Cheng
